wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Mossad reportedly warned Washington of explosive drones aimed at Trump. Within days Iran's Guard said mines had hit tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and after the US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran struck Bahrain and an airbase used by US forces in Kuwait, so the Gulf states that host those forces now take the return fire.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in 24 hours, but more crude reached the market by other routes. Iraq reopened the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey after a decade, and Russia's crude shipments hit their highest since late July as drone strikes on its refineries left more oil to export.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The slide came as Trump called a new Iran offensive highly unlikely and Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August. Brent jumped to $94.30 minutes after a Trump post on Iran, then Iran said mines hit 4 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in 24 hours, while Russia's crude shipments climbed to their highest since late July.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news came from the Gulf: an LNG carrier exploded in Hormuz, Russian state news agency TASS reported only 2 LNG tankers crossed the strait last week, and the IMF said Qatar's economy will shrink more than 14%. None of it concerns US supply or demand, and none of it accounts for this price on its own.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The fortnight brought a wheat ship that capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea-drone strike, with all 12 crew surviving, and Israel's war leaving 24% of Lebanon's wheatland fallow. Both came after this reading, and neither accounts for the price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news explains the price. Rice surfaced only at the edges: Thai inflation hit 3.9%, above the central bank's ceiling, and the UN urged Iran and the US to let fertilisers through Hormuz before millions sink into poverty.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Copper fell to $13,778 a tonne in early November, its lowest since July, on fears of an AI backlash around the midterms, a drop that lands after the chart's latest monthly reading. Miners still drew money: Adani agreed to finance Codelco's Kaburkaala exploration in northern Chile, and National Resources Limited reported copper and gold at Chagai.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and the Fed's minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes against an inflation pushed up by the oil shock. Logan called for two more, Daly for hikes outright, and Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December, naming the AI investment surge as a source of overheating.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The slide began with the chipmakers that had carried it: after the midterms' blue wave and a backlash against data centres, Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% in one session. The selling crossed to Asia the next day, where South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The selloff in AI stocks spread far enough that South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%, dragging down SK Hynix and TSMC. Then Nvidia was hit by reports that its board may oust Jensen Huang over an affair he confessed to staff by email, and its futures fell nearly 12%.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war oil shock that priced out demand is unwinding unevenly: Russia's crude shipments hit their highest since late July as drone strikes on its refineries left more crude to export, and Pakistan cut diesel to Rs364 a litre, still above the pre-war Rs281. The US meanwhile raised its forecasts for 2027 gasoline and diesel prices.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Liquefied gas from the Gulf has nearly stopped moving: Bloomberg tracking, reported by TASS, counted 2 LNG carriers through Hormuz in the week to 17 November, after Iran's navy said one hit a mine. A drone attack also suspended production at Iraq's Khor Mor gasfield, and the IEA said $40bn of pipelines will not end the Gulf's Hormuz dependence.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: Nvidia spent the fortnight in a leadership crisis after Jensen Huang's exit, even as it forecast $130 billion in Q4 revenue, and the Fed's Barr warned that AI agents could fuel future bank runs. Both came after the early-November peak, and nothing here accounts for it.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan's external accounts got news in both directions: the Asian Development Bank approved a $500M pension-reform loan, while the Hormuz closure cut mango export earnings from $100 million to $60 million. Neither is large enough to account for the rupee's path.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's Nigerian news centred on Tinubu's oil-backed borrowing: 340 million barrels of future crude reportedly pledged against 11.2 trillion naira, which Atiku would review to subsidise petrol. None of it accounts for the naira's slide.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo spent the fortnight raising hard currency: a decree pledged 112 million square metres of Red Sea coast against public debt, the state began paying on the spot for gold from Aswan's informal miners, and IMF staff agreed to release $2.3bn. All three came after most of the pound's firming, and none of it accounts for that.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Gold fell 6.4% in 7 days in mid-November, thinning the cushion Turkish households keep against a falling lira. None of the fortnight's other Turkish news, from the Habaş steel plant blast in Aliağa to Iraq reopening the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline, accounts for the exchange rate itself.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Bangladesh in this window was political: Sheikh Hasina applied for a passport to return from India, paramilitary units deployed nationwide, and arsonists hit 37 Grameen Bank branches since 10 November. None of it reported anything about the dollar flows that set this rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The slide came from Washington more than Jakarta: bets on the Fed lifted the dollar and pushed the rupiah to a record low. At home, Prabowo was reported to have accepted his vice president's resignation, a political shock landing on a currency already under pressure.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight brought Lebanon's army seizing a weapons depot in Beirut's southern suburbs, and word that Israel's war left 24% of Lebanon's wheatland in the Bekaa Valley fallow. Nothing reported touched the central bank or the dollar market, and neither story accounts for the rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news explains the rate's drift. What it carried was the yuan's widening reach: China's central bank says nearly 30% of goods trade now settles in yuan, as sanctions on Russia and Iran push traders off dollar payments, and HKEX launched an index of 305 offshore yuan bonds.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed as India's trade picture improved: exports surged 30% in October and the trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion, so fewer dollars had to be bought to pay for imports. Retail inflation hit 6.09% in the same month, a two-year high that breached the ceiling.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The slide followed Lula's win, after which Bloomberg reported Brazil's investor class had cooled on him. It ran through a fight over the fiscal gap: October inflation came in at 4.63%, and the Senate passed the government's fiscal adjustment bill with 45 votes without halting the real's fall.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso weakened after Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stopped migrant caravans, a threat set off by 1,500 migrants walking north from Tapachula. A week later it fell to a 17-month low as the Fed outlook made dollar assets more attractive than peso ones.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The dollar bought more euros as France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points and the European Central Bank made clear it would leave that gap to markets rather than step in. Washington's yen intervention also ran through the euro: it sold $500 million of euros to buy yen.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, and Washington then sold $500 million of euros for yen as the currency breached 160. October core inflation of 2.2% has cemented a Bank of Japan hike in December, but a board split on how far rates should go has kept sellers testing the line Tokyo defends.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Drone strikes on Russian refineries left more crude to sell abroad, and shipments reached their highest since late July, the kind of export earnings the ruble trades on. Brussels sanctioned the Wildberries founder and proposed a €45 billion Ukraine loan tied to Russian reparations. Neither explains the currency's path.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The South African Reserve Bank held the repo rate at 7.25%, but 3 of 7 rate-setters voted to hike, and Lesetja Kganyago named a firm dollar, fuel and a possible Fed hike as the risks widening inflation. A weaker rand carries all three into prices, because it raises the local cost of imported fuel.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The slide came in waves of forced selling: $1.26 billion of leveraged bets were liquidated as tech stocks fell, then $1.3 billion more in 24 hours. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $1.282 billion in a week, and MSCI dropped Strategy, owner of 850,364 bitcoin, from its indexes, putting its bitcoin-buying model on the line.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ether fell with bitcoin, which broke below $75,000 and then $65,000 this month, with miners leading Wall Street's crypto sell-off. Ethereum's developers then pushed the Glamsterdam upgrade into 2027, after an Ethereum Foundation developer counted 15,000 contracts it would break.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The slide followed traders' bets that the Fed would raise rates rather than cut them. A firm dollar and the cost of holding a metal that pays no interest pushed gold down, and an AI selloff in equities deepened this week's fall. In Turkey, where households keep savings in gold as a hedge against the lira, the drop wiped out the cushion many relied on.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A second car bomb in two days hit Moscow, injuring Sergei Zavorotny, a former adviser to Mykola Azarov. Putin then sat down with Trump and Xi in Shenzhen, where the three-power declaration named no war. Meanwhile Ukraine's drones hit the Crimean Bridge at Kerch, and Russia struck two bridges and the subway in Kyiv.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Rezaei said the strait will remain closed until Iran's seven conditions are met, and Iran's Guard and navy then said mines had hit tankers, 4 in 24 hours. Only 2 liquefied natural gas tankers crossed last week, and Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao put the cost of insuring one transit at $64m.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and a projectile struck another as it left the strait. Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao puts the insurance on a single transit at $64m, so owners are staying out. Qatar's LNG shipments have nearly stopped, and the IMF expects its economy to shrink more than 14% this year.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: A Japanese container ship transited the strait for the first time in three years on the same day Yemeni government forces withdrew and left the Houthis holding the Bab el-Mandeb coast. Houthi forces are now pressing on Aden, the seat of the internationally recognised government, while Saudi-led strikes hit Hodeidah.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The rise came as container lines began testing the Red Sea again: a Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab after three years away. The risk has not left the route. The Houthis have sent at least 3 small-arms shipments to Sudan's army and are courting Port Sudan, and the Iran war has already cut Egypt's Suez Canal revenue.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight accounts for Malacca's traffic. The shipping news was further west: Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and TASS reported that only 2 liquefied natural gas tankers crossed Hormuz last week.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's diplomacy around the strait, from Trump, Putin and Xi meeting in Shenzhen to the Quad's critical-minerals deals in Manila, said nothing about shipping through it, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic heading for the strait has been sailing through a war zone: drones reportedly hit at least 7 Black Sea ships last month, then 3 more inside Romanian waters near Sulina, and a wheat ship capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea-drone strike, its 12 crew rescued. The EU answered with €50 million to speed up a Black Sea security hub.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight brought an EU boarding of a Russian "shadow fleet" tanker, Storm Charles cancelling more than 300 flights in Portugal, and a general strike in Spain that unions say 90% of port and auto workers joined. None of it is tied to traffic through the strait itself.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: A Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab after three years, taking the Red Sea route this detour replaced. One sailing does not account for the dip, and the same day the Houthis, whose attacks emptied that route, said they had targeted King Khalid Airport in Riyadh with missiles.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Ukraine's strikes on the bridge over the strait came after this reading. Drones hit it first, a second strike within 24 hours dropped the road span, and satellite imagery then showed at least 2 Neptune hits on the rail span, Russia's main land supply route into occupied Crimea. None of that reaches the vessel counts here yet.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's data centre build-out, $94.67 billion of investment approved by its trade ministry since 2021, came under scrutiny in the Nvidia fallout as the U.S. further restricted China's access to AI chips, and Anwar's China line triggered a quiet investment freeze from Taiwan. None of it is tied directly to the index's fall.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Two shocks landed in mid-November. Prabowo was said to have accepted the resignation of his vice president, and the rupiah fell to a record low as Fed bets lifted the dollar, which shrinks what foreign holders of Jakarta shares get back. Neither story dates from the steepest leg of the fall, earlier in the month.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The AI rout that halted trading in South Korea after an 8% Kospi fall spread across Asia. Japan then spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, with Washington joining, and 2.2% core inflation cemented a Bank of Japan hike, both threatening the weak yen nearly half of Japan's manufacturers had just raised profit forecasts on.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's news from its largest names was about AI spending and new listings: Tencent's capital spending jumped 528% amid chip curbs, JD.com returned to profit, and Alibaba, Kuaishou and Adaspace lined up chip, video and satellite businesses for Hong Kong listings. None of it explains the slide.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The fortnight's China stories carried a yuan that has gained 9% on the euro and is squeezing exporters in Ningbo, factory prices rising 5.7%, the most since June 2022, and Washington pressing Beijing to carry out its Busan commitments. None of them is reported as the cause of the index's fall.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The AI rout reached Seoul: South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%, as the selloff spread across Asia through SK Hynix, TSMC and the Nikkei. The Nvidia crisis clouding the chip race hit the memory makers that dominate the index, even as SK Hynix pressed ahead with its first fab in Yongin.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight brought two Indian figures pulling opposite ways. October exports jumped 30%, narrowing the trade deficit to $20.09 billion, while retail inflation reached 6.09%, a two-year high above the ceiling. Neither accounts for the climb on its own.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's news this fortnight centred on the US criminal probe into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, and on new US curbs on China's access to AI chips. Nothing reported ties either one to the banks and property firms that weight the index.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The AI rout that spread to Asia reached an index this tied to TSMC, and South Korea halted trading the same day after the Kospi fell 8%. Political risk followed: Xi pledged Taiwan's reunification, and a day later China staged unannounced Pacific drills that officials called 'silent intimidation' of Taiwan.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Canberra moved to create an AI regulator after an OpenAI agent's breach, and Coles disclosed a cyber attack without saying what happened. Neither moves an index this size. The one market shock in the period was two-year Treasury yields jumping 18 basis points on half-point Fed hike risk, and nothing here ties the fall to it.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The South African Reserve Bank held the repo rate the day after this reading, with 3 of 7 rate-setters voting to hike from 7.25% as fuel and a firm dollar widened inflation risks. A week earlier, Woolworths Foods turnover grew only 1.9%. Neither accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Nothing in the news from Brasília accounts for the October slide; what followed bore on the rates this index answers to. The central bank said inflation had passed the top of its target range while growth slowed, October consumer prices rose 4.63%, below forecasts, and 45 senators passed the government's fiscal adjustment bill.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans were stopped, after 1,500 migrants set out walking north from Tapachula. That threat lands on the US demand Mexican exporters depend on. A week later the peso hit a 17-month low on the Fed outlook.

mkt:byma.standing: Argentina's main stock index, on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos in Buenos Aires. Priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years: daily direction counts, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's Argentine news was Pope Leo's first visit, Javier Milei's refusal to recognise Lula's election win, and Iran listing the Navy and Air Force as terrorist organisations. None of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The war premium on US sour crude vanished as supply surged, a direct hit to an index this heavy in oil producers. Trade with the US stayed unresolved: Carney said only US policy shifts could change Canada's stance, and that Canada could work with Chinese automakers if talks failed.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes, and Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December. Dearer money lowers what future profits are worth today. Nvidia doubled profit to $65.3 billion, but it did so without Jensen Huang, whose fall from the company ran through the fortnight.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: UK inflation accelerated again, keeping it above target for more than two years. JP Morgan estimated a 1.4 million barrel-a-day oil surplus in October, which is bad news for the oil majors that weigh heavily on London. None of the reporting ties either event directly to the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Two of its own members carried the bad news: Mercedes-Benz halted investment in Germany after four months of talks, with its labour officials pledging to fight plant closures, and Deutsche Bank shares dropped on a leak of 15 million files showing it kept about 28,000 flagged clients. Brussels meanwhile cleared UniCredit's €45 billion bid for Commerzbank, another member.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: French politics is the backdrop: Ifop puts Le Pen at 32-36% and Mélenchon, who promised 20,000 supporters nationalisations and a NATO exit, at 17-19.5% as the centre stalls. France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points, and the European Central Bank has left France to markets.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Dutch news in the window was the race to replace Lagarde at the European Central Bank, where Knot faces De Cos, and a grid queue of 15,498 Dutch firms as data centres crowd out warehouses. Neither story accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight was dominated by its first general strike in 14 years, over housing, and by a Berlin deal giving Spain the European Central Bank presidency, with De Cos set to replace Lagarde. Neither story accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italy wants €5.9 billion from its banks next year, and Intesa has attacked the levy, a direct charge on the lenders that weigh most in this index. UniCredit's €45 billion bid for Commerzbank won unconditional EU approval, and ICEYE bid for Avio at a 21.3% premium. None of this accounts for the earlier fall.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss news was diplomatic, not corporate: the Russian Embassy said Swiss policy had buried the country's reputation as a mediator, and Moscow's envoy set out objections to Switzerland's OSCE chairmanship. None of it touches Nestlé, Roche or Novartis, or accounts for the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: Israel is between governments: the Knesset was sworn in with Benjamin Netanyahu holding the security services as caretaker without a majority, and Eisenkot is negotiating a unity coalition with him. The latest drop came as Israel launched its first large operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire and the Board of Peace warned the truce faced collapse.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump met Putin and Xi in Shenzhen, where the three issued a "peace declaration" that names no war. In Brooklyn, Asif Merchant received 330 months for plotting to kill him, and Fed governor Lisa Cook refused a White House hearing on her removal. None of it falls on the early-month peak.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts. The minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting showed almost all officials expecting more rate hikes. Daly now openly calls for them, Goolsbee leaves a larger-than-usual rise open for December, and Deutsche Bank expects three straight hikes.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The fortnight in Frankfurt was about who sets this rate, not where it sits: Lagarde leaves on 7 February, and Berlin's deal hands Spain the presidency and Germany the chief economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier. The ECB also declined to step in as France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points. None of it explains the rate's path.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: Hiring ran well ahead of what forecasters expected: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against 65,000 forecast. Prices rose only slightly over the same month, and Fed officials, Barkin among them, called the policy direction clear while urging a careful pace.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Silver went down with gold, which had its worst week since March as traders bet on a Fed rate hike. A firm dollar raised the cost of holding metals that pay no interest, and an AI selloff hit at the same time. Gold lost 8.9% on the week and touched $3,757, its lowest since September 2025.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: October's report showed inflation slowing less than expected, and the Fed's Goolsbee called it 'borderline disturbing'. Treasuries slid as traders cemented bets on a December rate hike, and Bitcoin dropped to almost a three-month low as the data dimmed risk appetite.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran's navy and Guard said mines disabled tankers on successive days, a projectile hit another leaving the strait, and Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao put the cost of insuring one transit at $64m. Only 2 LNG tankers crossed last week, TASS reported, while Iran shortened its reopening plan from 7 days to 2 in talks in Islamabad.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: A Japanese container ship transited the strait in mid-November for the first time in three years. The same day Yemen government forces withdrew from the coast, leaving the Houthis holding the Red Sea's southern chokepoint, and they have since pressed on Aden while their missiles struck Riyadh.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Yemeni government forces withdrew from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis holding the Red Sea's southern chokepoint, the gate every Suez-bound ship passes. In Cairo, an Iran war that has cut Suez Canal revenue sits behind the IMF's $2.3bn deal and a decree pledging 112 million square metres of Red Sea coast against debt.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The news out of Panama this fortnight was about Etesa's transmission contract, which addenda quadrupled in cost, and the bombing of reporter Rolando Rodríguez's home in Panama City. Neither touches the locks or accounts for the traffic.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's news came from the far end of that oil route: Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in Hormuz in 24 hours, and only 2 liquefied natural gas tankers crossed it last week. None of it accounts for the rise in ships through the Malacca Strait.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's news from the sea lanes came from the far end of the route. Iran says mines hit tankers in Hormuz, and Yemen government forces withdrew from Bab el-Mandeb, leaving the Houthis holding the Red Sea's southern chokepoint. None of it accounts for this strait's traffic.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, where the US pressed a new security framework for Europe, and Zelensky said the US had suggested Kyiv cede land for Nato entry. The strikes went on: Russia hit 2 bridges and the subway in Kyiv, partly cutting water and power, and Ukraine's drones struck the Crimean Bridge.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang resigned amid a US-China spy scandal over his ties to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, and Colette Kress, the finance chief since 2013, now runs Nvidia. Doubled profit of $65.3 billion and a $130bn quarter forecast, the first results without Huang, did not halt the selling.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple's iPhone AI in China now runs on Alibaba's Qwen, which powers Siri there, and an internal update at Apple knocked its services, Apple Pay among them, offline for a stretch this week. Neither story accounts for the share's climb.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: The fortnight's news about Google was about its own products and deals: a fourth Gemini 4 model in 7 weeks, a $10 billion purchase of Anthropic shares ahead of Anthropic's IPO, and a rule that Android will block apps from unregistered developers from January 2027. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon lost 40 of its Amazon Leo internet satellites when a United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket, the Boeing and Lockheed Martin venture, failed 10 minutes after liftoff. In Berlin, a study found Meta and Amazon paid under 9% tax in 2025. Neither event accounts for the share's swings.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Outlook and Teams went down for nearly a day, Downdetector logged 130,000 outage reports at the peak, and the shares fell 3% as the disruption ran on. That week a researcher leaked SignDrop, an exploit that gives ordinary Windows users System rights. Days earlier Nvidia fell 6.27%, briefly ceding second place to Microsoft.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX's tower caught Ship 42 after 14 orbits, its first catch of a Starship upper stage from orbit, two days after the company set out $74 billion in plans for AI computing campuses. Against that, the European Commission demanded Starshield be restored in Ukraine, where Zelenskyy says it caps drones at 161 kph, a claim SpaceX denies.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: The fortnight brought regulators rather than results: Italy fined Meta $880m over photo privacy, Brazil's electoral court fined Facebook for 9 days of missed court orders, and Meta shelved terms claiming training rights over its customers' websites. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: The Houthis claimed 6 strikes inside Saudi Arabia. Debris from intercepted missiles then blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, and an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, the line that carries crude across the kingdom. The Yemeni military has since named Aramco its prime target. None of this accounts for the share price.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla killed the Cybertruck after selling 11,586 in nine months, by Cox Automotive's estimate, and its shares jumped 4% that morning on what replaces it: the steering-wheel-free Cybercab, now open to orders from select customers. Bloomberg then reported merger talks with SpaceX, with an announcement put at December.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: The news about Samsung's own business was expansion, not a setback: it was in buyout talks for Modine, whose shares gained the most in six years on the report, and it was building for the AI boom. Neither accounts for the fall in its share price.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: The Bureau of Industry and Security licensed hundreds of thousands of advanced Nvidia and AMD GPUs to firms the Department of War lists as Chinese military companies. Few of the chips shipped, and Chinese clouds had already moved to domestic silicon, so the licences opened little; nothing reported ties them to the share's fall.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.
co:berkshire.recent: The one story in the window about Berkshire itself was Buffett giving 9 million of his own shares to family foundations. The gift changes who holds the stock, not what the company earns, and nothing in the input explains the climb in the share price.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Chase's own systems failed on Monday, when nearly 5,000 customers reported outages and Zelle transfers were delayed. Days later, hackers took customer data from JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard through a single shared third-party vendor. Neither event explains the longer slide that began weeks earlier.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: The fortnight carried SK Hynix's construction of its first fab at Yongin, a plant to stand 150 metres tall that Nikkei Asia described as a round-the-clock race to finish, but nothing in it accounts for the fall in the share price.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.
us-mortgage.recent: The one housing story in the window was the result rather than the cause: US home sales fell to their lowest level since 2016, as buyers met borrowing costs well above what most existing owners locked in. Nothing in the input explains the rate's own climb.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The slide bottomed on the day Bitcoin fell below $65,000 for the first time since August, and SOL went down with it. The one story about the token itself was about plumbing: VanEck dropped Gemini as custodian of its bitcoin, ether and SOL ETFs, which changes who holds the coins and does nothing to demand for them.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: XRP fell with the whole crypto market. An Nvidia-led tech selloff hit the crypto majors, US inflation data pushed Bitcoin to almost a three-month low, and outflows from Bitcoin ETFs mounted. As money left crypto, XRP reached its lowest price since November 2024.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The news from the exchange was about what trades on it, not the token itself: Nvidia futures there fell nearly 12% on reports the board may oust Jensen Huang, and a former Robinhood engineer pleaded guilty to an insider trading scheme on Hyperliquid. Neither accounts for the token's slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: UK inflation accelerated to 3.6% in October, leaving it above target for more than two years running. Four days earlier the Bank of England's chief economist said further rate rises were needed to combat inflation, turning the argument from how far to cut to whether to raise.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The case for another hike built through November. Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen as it slid toward 160 per dollar, and core inflation of 2.2% kept the hike in view despite missing the 2.3% forecast. Against it: Uniqlo reversed a sock price increase within days, a sign shoppers still resist higher prices.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.
tcmb-rate.recent: The one relevant item from the fortnight is the central bank raising its end-2027 inflation forecast to 21%, published after the latest reading. A higher inflation path argues for a slower pace of cuts, but nothing in the input explains the cut itself.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The fortnight brought no rate decision. The PBOC's visible work was on the currency instead: it held the yuan with a stable fix as volatility jumped after APEC, while Europe pressed for a stronger yuan and Reuters described one too weak abroad and too strong at home.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: Brazil's central bank is caught between two pressures: inflation has passed the top of its target range while growth slows. The bank names four separate shocks behind the overshoot, so it cannot ease to support a cooling economy without letting prices run further.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.
bi-rate.recent: The latest news on Indonesia's money concerned the currency rather than the rate: the rupiah fell to a record low as Fed bets boosted the dollar, the pressure that limits how far Bank Indonesia can cut. Nothing in it reports a rate decision.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The fortnight's headlines on the Bank of Russia covered its routine yuan purchases, its work with banks to expand digital ruble services and its ruling on which cryptocurrencies ordinary investors may buy, and none of them accounts for the rate.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Thai inflation accelerated to 3.9%, breaching the BOT target, and Siam Cement said its Hormuz-affected Vietnam plastics plant stays shut until mid-2027. Both point to an energy shock reaching Thai prices and one of the index's industrial heavyweights, though nothing in the input ties the slide to either directly.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The Houthi war reached Riyadh. A strike on the airport killed at least 13 on 10 October. Debris from intercepted missiles then blew out windows across Aramco Tower, and an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze. Against that, Saudi Arabia reported oil output up 26% in October, ahead of an OPEC capacity audit that sets 2027 quotas.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Trump signalled after a Qatar meeting that new Iran strikes were unnecessary, which eased the war risk hanging over Gulf assets. Next door, AD Ports' quarterly profit jumped 73% as ships rerouted around the Hormuz closure. None of the reports ties Dubai's own listings to either event directly.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's fortnight was dominated by the ASEAN summit, a trade deal Trump announced with the Philippines, and new Quad critical-mineral deals. None of it accounts for the slide in local shares.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Italy fined Meta $880m over photo privacy, and Brazil fined Facebook for 9 days of missed court orders during its election. Meta shelved terms claiming training rights over its customers' websites, Jason Wei quit its TBD Lab after about a year, and its Muse assistant was found role-playing sex as a real, named woman.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent's quarterly capital spending jumped 528% to 81.4 billion yuan while it expanded Hy4 inference capacity tenfold on WorkBuddy demand. It then priced Hy4 flash at $0.07 per million input tokens, a 95% cut, and launched an AI search engine that indexes WeChat accounts. None of that reporting is given as the reason for the share's fall.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Jensen Huang left Nvidia after a 'confession' email about an affair tied to Megaspeed, a Singapore firm now under criminal probe over chip diversion to China. Shareholders sued, alleging investors were misled, and Washington closed a remote AI chip loophole. Without Huang, Nvidia still doubled profit to $65.3 billion.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: The fall predates the news about Google's own business, and none of that news accounts for the price. Google shipped Gemini 4 Hydrogen and then Neon, set Android to block apps from unregistered developers from January 2027, won a judge's approval to buy Spirit Airlines' passenger data, and bought $10 billion of Anthropic alongside Nvidia.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: Houthi missiles reached Riyadh again and again: debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower and later fell on the capital, and the Houthis claimed King Khalid Airport as a target. An unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze. The Saudi coalition answered with strikes on 60 Houthi military sites as Houthi forces pushed toward Aden.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: The US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran answered with fire on an airbase in Kuwait and repeated strikes on Bahrain, which hosts US forces. Peace talks stalled; in Islamabad, Iran shortened its Hormuz reopening plan from 7 days to 2, and a third US carrier reached the Gulf.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Nigeria's electoral commission blamed 54 officials for fake voter records, and Ezekwesili demanded an independent investigation of the register. In Gombe, armed men blocked Isa Pantami's convoy with burning tyres. None of it concerns Obi's own campaign or accounts for what traders paid.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months, but the word out of Abu Dhabi was that Putin is not ready to make peace. Since then Russia has hit 2 bridges and the subway in Kyiv, Ukrainian drones struck the Crimean Bridge at Kerch, and Putin vowed 'much more painful' strikes.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: The US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran answered with strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain as a third US carrier reached the Gulf. Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and its shortened Hormuz reopening plan, floated in Islamabad, has not restarted stalled peace talks.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: The Indian items in the feed were protests against the Modi government, including one at Jantar Mantar. None of them concerned Gyanesh Kumar, and nothing in the input accounts for what traders are paying.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: The fortnight brought Iranian strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain after the US hit Qeshm Island, tankers Iran says were mined in the Strait of Hormuz, and a third US carrier in the Persian Gulf. None of it touched the treaty itself, and nothing in it accounts for the price.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The fortnight's escalation came by air and sea: the US struck Qeshm Island, Iran answered with drones on Bahrain and an airbase used by US forces in Kuwait, a third US carrier reached the Gulf, and Iran said mines hit tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. None of it put US troops on Iranian soil, and none of it accounts for the earlier slide.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The fighting widened instead of ending: the US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran answered with attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain, and a third US carrier reached the Gulf, bringing 3 carriers and 13 destroyers to face Iran. Iran's offer in Islamabad to reopen Hormuz in 2 days rather than 7 stalled with the talks, while its Guard said mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: Israel launched central Gaza's first large operation since the ceasefire, and the Board of Peace, the truce's overseer, warned it faced imminent collapse and blamed both Israel and Hamas. Days earlier an Israeli airstrike killed 6 people inside Nasser Hospital. The IDF called its push on a Hamas tunnel across the Yellow Line a one-day operation.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: The US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran answered by hitting an airbase in Kuwait and striking Bahrain again, with peace talks stalled. A third US carrier reached the Gulf, and Iran said mines hit four tankers in 24 hours.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts, and Logan called for two more rate hikes, possibly rapidly. Minutes of the October 27-28 meeting then showed almost all officials expected to tighten further, Daly openly called for hikes, and Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December.

poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Ukraine signs its EU accession treaty by 2027. Signing comes only after every negotiating chapter closes and all 27 member states agree, so the price is a bet on the pace of talks in Brussels.
poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's stories touched the accession treaty itself. They carried Russia and Ukraine's first peace talks in 9 months, Putin vowing 'much more painful' strikes, Zelensky saying the US had suggested Kyiv cede land for Nato entry, and Brussels proposing a €45 billion loan repayable only if Russia pays reparations.

poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Hegseth stops being the US Secretary of Defense before the end of the year. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reports about his standing at the Pentagon.

wiki-inflation.standing: The general rise in prices across an economy, usually measured by a consumer price index. Central banks set interest rates to keep it near a target, so its pace decides what borrowers and savers pay.
wiki-inflation.recent: October's price data ran hot in many economies: US consumer prices rose 0.4%, beating forecasts, India's retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high, and China's producer prices reached their highest since June 2022. The Fed's Logan called for two more rate hikes, and Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more.

wiki-china.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on China each day: a rough gauge of how often the world's second-largest economy and most populous one-party state pulls general readers toward the basics.
wiki-china.recent: Trump and Putin came to Shenzhen to meet Xi, and the three-power "peace declaration" they signed names no war. Prabowo met Xi there too, having visited China 4 times in 2 years. In the same week, China's central bank said nearly 30% of goods trade is now settled in yuan.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Houthis and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay on the war between Yemen's Houthi movement and the kingdom ending, and so on Red Sea and Gulf oil risk.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: Bets on a truce fell as the war reached the Saudi capital. Missile debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower, the Houthis claimed a strike on King Khalid Airport, and debris fell on Riyadh again as Houthi forces pushed toward Aden. The Saudi-led coalition answered with strikes on Hodeidah and on 60 Houthi military sites.

wiki-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps.standing: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is Iran's parallel military, founded after the 1979 revolution and answerable to the Supreme Leader. It runs the missile force, a navy in the Gulf and a large business empire.
wiki-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps.recent: Bahrain took its third Iranian drone attack in a week, aimed at a base hosting a US radar, while the Guard said tankers hit mines on its banned Hormuz route. France had blamed it for hacking freezers in 700 French supermarkets, and in Brooklyn Asif Merchant got 330 months for plotting to kill Donald Trump.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily reads of English Wikipedia's article on the United States, one of its most-visited country pages. It rises when American power or politics becomes the world's story, not only America's.
wiki-united-states.recent: Democrats reached 56 Senate seats on nine flipped races, Alaska's won by Peltola. The NY governor called for Sean Duffy's resignation after air travel chaos, and Asif Merchant received 330 months for plotting to kill Donald Trump. All of it came in November and none of it explains the October peak.

poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Bola Tinubu wins Nigeria's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay on a second term for the president of Africa's most populous country.
poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.recent: The fortnight's news from Nigeria's race was about the machinery, not the candidates: Nigeria's electoral commission blamed 54 officials for fake voter records, Ezekwesili demanded an independent investigation of the voter register, and armed men blocked Isa Pantami's convoy in Gombe. None of it accounts for the price.

stocks:MSFT.standing: Shares in the maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, one of the world's most valuable companies. Its OpenAI stake and its data-centre spending make it a bellwether for whether the AI build-out pays.
stocks:MSFT.recent: A server-capacity failure took Outlook and Teams down for nearly a day, with Downdetector logging 130,000 Outlook reports at the peak, and the shares fell 3% as the disruption spread. The same week a researcher leaked SignDrop, a Windows exploit that hands ordinary users System rights.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Iran ceasefire is still holding on 31 December. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on every strike, threat and report of talks.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The fighting since mid-November has run between Iran and the US, not Israel. After the US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran hit an airbase in Kuwait and struck Bahrain 4 times in 6 days, and says mines hit 4 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. A third US carrier reached the Gulf, and peace talks are stalled.

wiki-nvidia.standing: Nvidia, the Santa Clara chip designer whose graphics processors run most of the world's AI training, and one of the most valuable companies on earth. Its fortunes carry the chip sector and the data-centre build-out with them.
wiki-nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang left Nvidia after an email to staff confessed an affair with a Singapore-based company's CEO, amid a US-China spy scandal over Megaspeed, now under criminal probe for chip diversion.
